verdict.rationale: Pomelo ships its own natural-language tooling: an AI assistant for API questions and an official MCP server (installable in Cursor). The MCP server returns endpoints matching a Spanish or English query and generates request code, and the docs promise connecting to the APIs 'using natural language'. The documented tools only help with discovery and code generation; no tool is shown that actually runs operations such as issuing cards or blocking merchants from a natural-language command. Missing for 10: documented natural-language execution of product operations (cards, users, transactions), a list of action tools in the MCP server, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
